subject: P1/P2 SLA exception request — priority routing & night escalation roster

From: Finora Ops <ops@finora.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Latency incident and overnight response ask

Hi Irene,

Quick note — we saw a pattern of sustained 2–3x tail latency for generation calls between 02:00–04:00 UTC last night affecting a small subset of keys. Our SREs traced this to noisy batch sizing during a regional burst; impact was limited but triggered customer-visible errors for payment reconciliation jobs (P1 for us).

Given our launch window next week, Finora is asking whether Redwood can temporarily expand nighttime on-call coverage and accept a P1 response SLA exception for the next two weeks (we’d like guaranteed 30-minute acknowledgement for P1s overnight instead of the standard 60). We'll be happy to coordinate canary traffic and share a routing policy to minimize cost.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can: 
- Provision a temporary priority route that pins our keys to dedicated capacity between 02:00–05:00 UTC (or equivalent burst protection)?
- Provide a documented escalation roster and a named point-of-contact for overnight P1s?

Thanks — attaching the incident summary.

ALICIA PARK
Head of Ops, Finora Payments

Hi Alicia — thanks for the heads up and the incident summary. Sorry to hear the reconciliation jobs were impacted. We can support a short-term escalation/roster exception while we finalize longer-term capacity controls. Proposed immediate plan (high level):

1) Temporary priority route (2 weeks): Pin Finora traffic to a small dedicated pool during 02:00–05:00 UTC; this prevents noisy co-tenants from affecting tail latency.
2) Night escalation roster: Redwood will provide a 3-person on-call shadow for those hours with a 30-minute acknowledgement target for P1s and a 4-hour response target for P2s. The shadow will escalate to the normal oncall if the issue requires deeper runtime changes.
3) Canary and rollback: We want to run a gradual canary over first 12 hours and keep an automated fallback to the standard pool if error rates spike.

I’m attaching a draft roster and a short term-sheet for the SLA exception. Ben/Marcus — can you confirm capacity & cost delta for a 2-week pin and whether we have the headcount for a nightly shadow? Laura — can you draft the escalation contact block (names + phone) for Finora?

If Finora agrees, we can stand this up as a scoped exception and follow with a proposed quantized plan (batching/quantization) so this doesn't recur.

Thanks,

Irene Choi
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
